nodes.name: (ii),(iii): if $r_n\ge0$ then $x_{i
nodes.statement: (ii), (iii): If $r_{n}\geq 0$, then ${\bf r}\in \mathbb N^n$, and ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}^{{\bf r}}$ is a cluster monomial in ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ having the same $g$-vector  with the cluster variable $x_{i;t}$. By Theorem \ref{thmmonomial}, we get that $x_{i;t}={\bf x}_{t^\prime}^{{\bf r}}$. Then by Lemma \ref{lemvariable}, $x_{i;t}$ is a cluster variable in ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$. More precisely, if $r_{n}>0$, then $x_{i;t}=x_{n;t^{\prime}}$, and thus $d_{n}^\prime=-1$. If $r_{n}=0$, then $x_{i;t}=x_{k;t^\prime}$ for some $k\neq n$. In this case, $d_{n}^\prime=0$.
nodes.statement_short: (ii),(iii): if $r_n\ge0$ then $x_{i;t}$ is a variable of ${\bf x}_{t'}$

nodes.name: (iv): if $r_n<0$ then $d'_n>0$
nodes.statement: (iv): If $r_{n}<0$, then the exponent of $x_{n;t^\prime}$ in  ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}^{{\bf r}}$ is negative, and thus the minimal exponent of $x_{n;t^\prime}$ appearing in $f({\bf x}_{t^\prime})$ is negative. Recall that the meaning of $-d_{n}^\prime$ is just the minimal exponent of $x_{n;t^\prime}$ appearing in $f({\bf x}_{t^\prime})$. So $d_{n}^\prime$ is positive. The proof is finished.
nodes.statement_short: (iv): if $r_n<0$ then $d'_n>0$

nodes.name: Choose a g-pair partner along $[1,n]\setminus\{k\}$
nodes.statement: Let ${\bf x}_t$ be a cluster containing the cluster variable $x$. By Theorem \ref{thmenough}, we know that $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ has  the enough $g$-pairs property. Thus for $I=\{1,2,\cdots,n\}\backslash\{k\}$ and the cluster ${\bf x}_t$, there exists a cluster ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ such that $({\bf x}_t,{\bf x}_{t^\prime})$ is a $g$-pair along $I=\{1,2,\cdots,n\}\backslash\{k\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a g-pair partner along $[1,n]\setminus\{k\}$

nodes.name: Partner keeps $x_{k
nodes.statement:
Since ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$  is connected with ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ by an $I=\{1,2,\cdots,n\}\backslash\{k\}$-sequence, we know that $x_{k;t^\prime}=x_{k;t_0}$ and  $d_k=d_k^\prime$, by Proposition \ref{prodvectors}.
 Then the result follows  from $x_{k;t^\prime}=x_{k;t_0}$ and Lemma \ref{lemdv}.
nodes.statement_short: Partner keeps $x_{k;t_0}$ and $d_k$; apply Lemma 5.2

nodes.name: (i): supports agree via d-vectors and Corollary 5.3
nodes.statement:
(i). ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{\bf a}={\bf x}_{t_2}^{\bf f}$ can be viewed as the Laurent expansion of the cluster monomial ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{\bf a}$ with respect to the cluster ${\bf x}_{t_2}$. By this expansion, we know the $d$-vector of the cluster monomial ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{\bf a}$ is the vector $-{\bf f}\in \mathbb Z_{\leq 0}^n$. By Corollary \ref{thmdvectors}, for each $-f_j<0$, $x_{j;t_2}$ must be a cluster variable in support of ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{\bf a}$, i.e., each support cluster variable $x_{j;t_2}$ of ${\bf x}_{t_2}^{\bf f}$ is a support cluster variable of ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{\bf a}$.

Similarly, we can show each support cluster variable $x_{i;t_1}$ of ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{\bf f}$ is a support cluster variable of ${\bf x}_{t_2}^{\bf f}$, thus  ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{\bf a}$ and ${\bf x}_{t_2}^{\bf f}$ have the same support.
nodes.statement_short: (i): supports agree via d-vectors and Corollary 5.3

nodes.name: (ii): exponents agree by algebraic independence
nodes.statement:
(ii). If $x_{i;t_1}$ is not in the support of the two cluster monomials, then $a_i=f_j=0$.
If $x_{i;t_1}$ is a support cluster variable of the two cluster monomials, then $a_i=f_j$ follows from the algebraical independence of  cluster variables in the same cluster.
nodes.statement_short: (ii): exponents agree by algebraic independence

nodes.name: WLOG $I=\{1..p\}$
nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality, we can assume $I=\{1,2,\cdots,p\}$. Since both clusters ${\bf x}_{t_1},{\bf x}_{t_2}$ are connected with ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ by an $I$-sequence, we know that their $G$-matrices have the following form.
$$G_{t_1}=\begin{pmatrix}G(t_1)&0\\ W_1 &I_{n-p}\end{pmatrix}, G_{t_2}=\begin{pmatrix}G(t_2)&0\\ W_2&I_{n-p}\end{pmatrix},$$
where  $W_1, W_2$ are nonnegative matrices, by sign coherence of $G$-matrices.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $I=\{1..p\}$; block form of the partner G-matrices

nodes.name: Proposition 4.6 gives $Q_1,Q_2$ with $G(t_1)Q_1=G(t_2)Q_2$
nodes.statement: Because $({\bf x}_t,{\bf x}_{t_1})$ and $({\bf x}_t,{\bf x}_{t_2})$ are $g$-pairs along $I$ and by Proposition \ref{prodef}, there exist $Q_1,Q_2\in M_{p\times n}(\mathbb Z_{\geq0})$ such that $$G(t_1)Q_1=G_{t_1}|_{I\times I}Q_1=G_t|_{I\times [1,n]}=G_{t_2}|_{I\times I}Q_2=G(t_2)Q_2.$$
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 4.6 gives $Q_1,Q_2$ with $G(t_1)Q_1=G(t_2)Q_2$

nodes.name: Nonnegative matrices $A,F$ with $G_{t_1}A=G_{t_2}F$
nodes.statement:
It is easy to see that
 $$G_{t_1}\begin{pmatrix}Q_1\\W_2 Q_2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}G(t_1)&0\\ W_1 &I_{n-p}\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}Q_1\\W_2 Q_2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}G(t_2)&0\\ W_2&I_{n-p}\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}Q_2\\W_1 Q_1\end{pmatrix} =G_{t_2}\begin{pmatrix}Q_2\\W_1 Q_1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Note that $A=(a_{ij})_{n\times n}:=\begin{pmatrix}Q_1\\W_2 Q_2\end{pmatrix}$ and $F=(f_{ij})_{n\times n}:=\begin{pmatrix}Q_2\\W_1 Q_1\end{pmatrix}$ are non-negative matrices.
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegative matrices $A,F$ with $G_{t_1}A=G_{t_2}F$

nodes.name: Equal g-vectors give equal monomials and supports
nodes.statement: So the cluster monomials ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{{\bf a}_i}$ and ${\bf x}_{t_2}^{{\bf f}_i}$ have the same $g$-vectors for $i=1,\cdots,n$, where ${\bf a}_i, {\bf f}_i$ are $i$th column vectors of $A$ and $F$. By Theorem \ref{thmmonomial} and Proposition \ref{prosupport}, we get that ${\bf x}_{t_1}^{{\bf a}_i}$ and ${\bf x}_{t_2}^{{\bf f}_i}$ are equal and $Su({\bf x}_{t_1}^{{\bf a}_i})=Su({\bf x}_{t_2}^{{\bf f}_i})$ $i=1,\cdots,n$. Thus $\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^n Su({\bf x}_{t_1}^{{\bf a}_i})=\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^n Su({\bf x}_{t_2}^{{\bf f}_i})$.
nodes.statement_short: Equal g-vectors give equal monomials and supports

nodes.name: Full row rank shows the first $p$ variables are shared
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{detgthm},  we get that  $G_t|_{I\times [1,n]}$ is row full rank, so $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ do not zero rows. Thus $\{x_{1;t_1},\cdots,x_{p;t_1}\}\subseteq \bigcup\limits_{i=1}^n Su({\bf x}_{t_1}^{{\bf a}_i})\subseteq {\bf x}_{t_1}$ and $\{x_{1;t_2},\cdots,x_{p;t_2}\}\subseteq \bigcup\limits_{i=1}^n Su({\bf x}_{t_2}^{{\bf f}_i})\subseteq {\bf x}_{t_2}$. By $\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^n Su({\bf x}_{t_1}^{{\bf a}_i})=\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^n Su({\bf x}_{t_2}^{{\bf f}_i})$, we know that $\{x_{1;t_1},\cdots,x_{p;t_1}\}\subseteq {\bf x}_{t_2}$ and $\{x_{1;t_2},\cdots,x_{p;t_2}\}\subseteq {\bf x}_{t_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Full row rank shows the first $p$ variables are shared

nodes.name: Remaining variables are initial
nodes.statement: Since both clusters ${\bf x}_{t_1},{\bf x}_{t_2}$ are connected with ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ by an $I$-sequence, we know that $x_{k;t_1}=x_{k;t_0}=x_{k;t_2}$ for $k=p+1,\cdots,n$. Thus we must have ${\bf x}_{t_1}={\bf x}_{t_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Remaining variables are initial; clusters coincide

nodes.name: (i): equality of variables is coefficient-independent
nodes.statement:
(i). Since $B_{t_0}(1)=B_{t_0}(2)$, we know that $B_{t}(1)=B_{t}(2)$ for any $t\in\mathbb T_n$.
Let $\mathcal A(\mathcal S^{pr})$ be the skew-symmetrizable cluster algebra with principal coefficients at $t_1$ and with initial exchange matrix $B_{t_1}(1)=B_{t_1}(2)$.
The seed of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S^{pr})$ at $t\in\mathbb T_n$ is denoted by $({\bf x}_t^{pr},{\bf y}_t^{pr},B_{t}^{pr})$.

If $x_{i;t_1}(1)=x_{j;t_2}(1)$, we know that $d^{t_1}(x_{j;t_2}(1))=-{\bf e}_i$, where ${\bf e}_i$ is the $i$-th column vector of $I_n$. Since the $d$-vectors do not depend on the choice of coefficients, we know that $d^{t_1}(x_{j;t_2}^{pr})=-{\bf e}_i$. Then by Corollary \ref{thmdvectors}, we have that $x_{i;t_1}^{pr}=x_{j;t_2}^{pr}$.
Thus we obtain that $x_{i;t_1}(2)=x_{j;t_2}(2)$ from Theorem 3.7 of \cite{FZ3}.
By the same argument, we can show that if $x_{i;t_1}(2)=x_{j;t_2}(2)$, then $x_{i;t_1}(1)=x_{j;t_2}(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: (i): equality of variables is coefficient-independent

nodes.name: Same exchange matrices
nodes.statement:
Since $B_{t_0}(1)=B_{t_0}(2)$, we know that $B_{t}(1)=B_{t}(2)$ for any $t\in\mathbb T_n$.
Let $\mathcal A(\mathcal S^{pr})$ be the skew-symmetrizable cluster algebra with principal coefficients at $t_1$ and with initial exchange matrix $B_{t_1}(1)=B_{t_1}(2)$.
The seed of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S^{pr})$ at $t\in\mathbb T_n$ is denoted by $({\bf x}_t^{pr},{\bf y}_t^{pr},B_{t}^{pr})$.
nodes.statement_short: Same exchange matrices; introduce the principal-coefficient algebra

nodes.name: d-vector $-e_i$ transfers to principal coefficients
nodes.statement: If $x_{i;t_1}(1)=x_{j;t_2}(1)$, we know that $d^{t_1}(x_{j;t_2}(1))=-{\bf e}_i$, where ${\bf e}_i$ is the $i$-th column vector of $I_n$. Since the $d$-vectors do not depend on the choice of coefficients, we know that $d^{t_1}(x_{j;t_2}^{pr})=-{\bf e}_i$. Then by Corollary \ref{thmdvectors}, we have that $x_{i;t_1}^{pr}=x_{j;t_2}^{pr}$.
nodes.statement_short: d-vector $-e_i$ transfers to principal coefficients; Corollary 5.3

nodes.name: Transfer to the second algebra by FZ Theorem 3.7
nodes.statement:
Thus we obtain that $x_{i;t_1}(2)=x_{j;t_2}(2)$ from Theorem 3.7 of \cite{FZ3}.
By the same argument, we can show that if $x_{i;t_1}(2)=x_{j;t_2}(2)$, then $x_{i;t_1}(1)=x_{j;t_2}(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer to the second algebra by FZ Theorem 3.7; symmetric argument

nodes.name: (ii): seeds determined by clusters (GSV, FZ)
nodes.statement:
(ii). By (i), we know if there exists a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\cdots,n\}$ such that $x_{i;t_1}(1)=x_{\sigma(i);t_2}(1)$ for $i=1,\cdots,n$, then $x_{i;t_1}^{pr}=x_{\sigma(i);t_2}^{pr}$ for any $i$.
Then by \cite[Theorem 4]{GSV}, we have $y_{i;t_1}^{pr}=y_{\sigma(i);t_2}^{pr}$ and $b_{ij}^{t_1}(pr)=b_{\sigma(i)\sigma(j)}^{t_2}(pr)$. Then the result follows from \cite[Theorem 4.6]{FZ3}.
nodes.statement_short: (ii): seeds determined by clusters (GSV, FZ)

nodes.name: Fix the variables $x_{p+1
nodes.statement:
For the cluster variables $x_{p+1;t_0},\cdots,x_{n;t_0}$ of the cluster ${\bf x}_{t_0}$, we consider the seeds of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ whose clusters contain these variables. We need to check that if these seeds form a connected subgraph of the exchange graph of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$.

Thanks to Proposition \ref{proclustervariable}, we can assume that $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ is a cluster algebra with principal coefficients at $t_0$. Let ${\bf x}_t$ be a cluster containing the variables  $x_{p+1;t_0},\cdots,x_{n;t_0}$.
 Without  loss of generality, we can assume that $x_{i;t}=x_{i;t_0}$ for $i=p+1,\cdots,n$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the variables $x_{p+1;t_0},...,x_{n;t_0}$; reduce to principal coefficients

nodes.name: Take the g-pair partner along $\{1..p\}$
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{thmenough}, we know that $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ has  the enough $g$-pairs property. Thus for $I=\{1,2,\cdots, p\}$ and the cluster ${\bf x}_t$, there exists a cluster ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ such that $({\bf x}_t,{\bf x}_{t^\prime})$ is a $g$-pair along $I$. We will show that ${\bf x}_t={\bf x}_t^\prime$, thus ${\bf x}_t$ is connected with ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ by a $\{1,2,\cdots,p\}$-sequence.
nodes.statement_short: Take the g-pair partner along $\{1..p\}$

nodes.name: Partner monomial for each $x_{k
nodes.statement:
Since $({\bf x}_t,{\bf x}_{t^\prime})$ is a $g$-pair along $I$, we know that for the cluster variable $x_{k;t}$ (as a cluster monomial in ${\bf x}_t$), there exists a cluster monomial ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}^{{\bf v}}$ in ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}$ with $v_i=0$  for $i\notin I$ such that
$$\pi_I(g(x_{k;t}))=\pi_I(g({\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}^{{\bf v}}))=\pi_I(G_{t^{\prime}}{\bf v}).$$
nodes.statement_short: Partner monomial for each $x_{k;t}$

nodes.name: Block forms of the G-matrices
nodes.statement:
We know that the $G$-matrix of ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ has the form of $G_{t^{\prime}}=\begin{pmatrix}G(t^{\prime})&0\\ \ast& I_{n-p}\end{pmatrix}$. By the assumption, the $G$-matrix of ${\bf x}_t$ also has the form of $G_{t}=\begin{pmatrix}G(t)&0\\ \star& I_{n-p}\end{pmatrix}$.
By row sign-coherence of $G$-matrices, we know that both $\ast$ and $\star$ are nonnegative matrices.
nodes.statement_short: Block forms of the G-matrices; sign-coherence makes the lower blocks nonnegative

nodes.name: Pad both monomials to equal g-vectors
nodes.statement_short: Pad both monomials to equal g-vectors

nodes.name: Theorem 3.2: the padded monomials are equal
nodes.statement: This means that the cluster monomials $x_{k;t}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t}^{g_i^{\prime}}$ and ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}^{{\bf v}}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t^{\prime}}^{g_i}$ have the same $g$-vector. By Theorem \ref{thmmonomial}, we get that $$x_{k;t}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t}^{g_i^{\prime}}={\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}^{{\bf v}}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t^{\prime}}^{g_i}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 3.2: the padded monomials are equal

nodes.name: Supports give ${\bf x}_t={\bf x}_{t'}$, hence connectedness
nodes.statement:
By Proposition \ref{prosupport}, we know that $x_{k;t}$ is a cluster variable in ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$.
 Since $k$ is arbitrary, we obtain that ${\bf x}_{t}$ and ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}$ have the same cluster variables. So ${\bf x}_t$
is connected with ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ by a $\{1,2,\cdots,p\}$-sequence. By Proposition \ref{proclustervariable} (ii) or \cite[Theorem 4]{GSV}, each seed of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ is determined by its cluster, we know that the seed containing ${\bf x}_{t}$ and the seed containing ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ are connected by a $\{1,\cdots,p\}$-sequence and each seed appearing in this sequence containing the cluster variables $x_{p+1;t_0},\cdots,x_{n;t_0}$. So the seeds of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ whose clusters contain particular cluster variables form a connected subgraph of the exchange graph of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$.
nodes.statement_short: Supports give ${\bf x}_t={\bf x}_{t'}$, hence connectedness

nodes.name: (i): independence via Theorem 6.2 and Proposition 2.8
nodes.statement:
(i). Let ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ be another cluster of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ containing $x_{k;t_0}$, and $d^{t^\prime}(x_{i;t})=(d_1^\prime,\cdots,d_n^\prime)^{\top}$ be the $d$-vector of $x_{i;t}$ with respect to ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$.
 Without loss of generality, we can assume that $x_{k;t^\prime}=x_{k;t_0}$. By Theorem \ref{corconnected}, the cluster ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ is connected with ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ by a $\{1,2,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{k\}$-sequence.
 Then by Proposition \ref{prodvectors}, we get that $d_k^\prime=d_k$.
nodes.statement_short: (i): independence via Theorem 6.2 and Proposition 2.8

nodes.name: (ii): values of $d_k$
nodes.statement:
(ii). $d_k\geq -1$ follows from Corollary  \ref{thmdvectors} directly. The important thing is when $d_k$ takes values at $-1,0$, a positive integer.


 By Proposition \ref{prodrec}, we know that the notion of $d$-vectors is independent of the choice of coefficient system. Thanks to Proposition \ref{proclustervariable}, we can assume that  $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ is a skew-symmetrizable cluster algebra with principal coefficients at $t_0$.




(a). If  $x_{i;t}=x_{k;t_0}$, clearly, $d_k=-1$. Conversely, if $d_k=-1$, then $x_{i;t}=x_{k;t_0}$ follows from  Corollary \ref{thmdvectors} (i).


(b). By Corollary  \ref{thmdvectors}, if $d_k=0$, then there exists a cluster ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}$ containing both $x_{i;t}$ and $x_{k;t_0}$. Since $d_k=0$, we must have $x_{i;t}\neq x_{k;t_0}$.

Conversely, suppose that $x_{i;t}\neq x_{k;t_0}$ and there exists a cluster ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}$ containing both $x_{i;t}$ and $x_{k;t_0}$. Without loss of generality, we can assume that $x_{i;t}=x_{1;t^\prime}$ and $x_{k;t_0}=x_{2;t^\prime}$.
By (i), we know that $d_k$ does not depend on the cluster containing $x_{k;t_0}=x_{2;t^\prime}$, so $d_k$ is equal to the $2$-th component of $d^{t^\prime}(x_{i;t})$. Since $d^{t^\prime}(x_{i;t})=d^{t^\prime}(x_{1;t^{\prime}})=-{\bf e}_1$, we get $d_k=0$.


(c). By (a) and (b), $d_k\leq 0$ if and only if there exists a cluster containing both $x_{i,t}$ and $x_{k,t_0}$. So $d_k>0$ if and only if there exists no cluster containing both $x_{i,t}$ and $x_{k,t_0}$.

(d). We have proved that $d_k\geq -1$, and if $d_k=-1$, then $x_{i;t}\in {\bf x}_{t_0}$.
So if $x_{i;t}\notin{\bf x}_{t_0}$, then each $d_k$ is nonnegative, and we thus $d^{t_0}(x_{i;t})\in\mathbb N^n$.
The proof is finished.
nodes.statement_short: (ii): values of $d_k$

nodes.name: $d_k\ge-1$ from Corollary 5.3
nodes.statement: $d_k\geq -1$ follows from Corollary  \ref{thmdvectors} directly. The important thing is when $d_k$ takes values at $-1,0$, a positive integer.
nodes.statement_short: $d_k\ge-1$ from Corollary 5.3

nodes.name: Reduce to principal coefficients
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prodrec}, we know that the notion of $d$-vectors is independent of the choice of coefficient system. Thanks to Proposition \ref{proclustervariable}, we can assume that  $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ is a skew-symmetrizable cluster algebra with principal coefficients at $t_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to principal coefficients

nodes.name: (a): $d_k=-1$ iff $x_{i
nodes.statement: (a). If  $x_{i;t}=x_{k;t_0}$, clearly, $d_k=-1$. Conversely, if $d_k=-1$, then $x_{i;t}=x_{k;t_0}$ follows from  Corollary \ref{thmdvectors} (i).

nodes.name: (b): $d_k=0$ iff distinct and compatible
nodes.statement:
(b). By Corollary  \ref{thmdvectors}, if $d_k=0$, then there exists a cluster ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}$ containing both $x_{i;t}$ and $x_{k;t_0}$. Since $d_k=0$, we must have $x_{i;t}\neq x_{k;t_0}$.

Conversely, suppose that $x_{i;t}\neq x_{k;t_0}$ and there exists a cluster ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}$ containing both $x_{i;t}$ and $x_{k;t_0}$. Without loss of generality, we can assume that $x_{i;t}=x_{1;t^\prime}$ and $x_{k;t_0}=x_{2;t^\prime}$.
By (i), we know that $d_k$ does not depend on the cluster containing $x_{k;t_0}=x_{2;t^\prime}$, so $d_k$ is equal to the $2$-th component of $d^{t^\prime}(x_{i;t})$. Since $d^{t^\prime}(x_{i;t})=d^{t^\prime}(x_{1;t^{\prime}})=-{\bf e}_1$, we get $d_k=0$.
nodes.statement_short: (b): $d_k=0$ iff distinct and compatible

nodes.name: (c): $d_k>0$ iff no common cluster
nodes.statement: (c). By (a) and (b), $d_k\leq 0$ if and only if there exists a cluster containing both $x_{i,t}$ and $x_{k,t_0}$.
nodes.statement_short: (c): $d_k>0$ iff no common cluster

nodes.name: (d): positivity of d-vectors
nodes.statement:
(d). We have proved that $d_k\geq -1$, and if $d_k=-1$, then $x_{i;t}\in {\bf x}_{t_0}$.
So if $x_{i;t}\notin{\bf x}_{t_0}$, then each $d_k$ is nonnegative, and we thus $d^{t_0}(x_{i;t})\in\mathbb N^n$.
The proof is finished.
nodes.statement_short: (d): positivity of d-vectors

nodes.name: Repeat the known proof
nodes.statement: In order to make the readers to have a good sense of the proper Laurent monomial property, we repeat the proof  here.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the known proof
nodes.section: 6.3 Positivity, $d$-vectors and linear independence of cluster monomials

nodes.name: Expand a vanishing combination in ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ as $\Sigma
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\sum\limits_{t, {\bf v}} c_{t,{\bf v}}{\bf x}_t^{\bf v}=0$, where ${\bf v}\in\mathbb N^n, c_{t,{\bf v}}\in\mathbb {ZP}$. Fix a cluster ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ and a ${\bf v}_0\in \mathbb N^n$, by the proper Laurent monomial property,  each ${\bf x}_t^{\bf v}\notin CM(t_0)$ is a sum of proper Laurent monomials in $\mathbb{ZP}[x_{1;t_0}^{\pm1},\cdots,x_{n;t_0}^{\pm1}]$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand a vanishing combination in ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ as $\Sigma_1+\Sigma_2$
nodes.section: 6.3 Positivity, $d$-vectors and linear independence of cluster monomials

nodes.name: Coefficient comparison gives $c_{t_0,{\bf v}_0}=0$
nodes.statement:
The coefficient of ${\bf x}_{t_0}^{{\bf v}_0}$  in $\Sigma_1$, as well as in $\Sigma_1+\Sigma_2$, is precisely $c_{t_0,{\bf v}_0}$.
  Then, $\Sigma_1+\Sigma_2=0$ results in $c_{t_0,{\bf v}_0}=0$.
 And thus cluster monomials of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ are linearly independent
over $\mathbb {ZP}$.
nodes.statement_short: Coefficient comparison gives $c_{t_0,{\bf v}_0}=0$
nodes.section: 6.3 Positivity, $d$-vectors and linear independence of cluster monomials

nodes.name: Reduce to the proper Laurent monomial property via Theorem 6
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{lemproper}, it suffices to show the positivity of cluster variables and the positivity of $d$-vectors imply the proper Laurent monomial property.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the proper Laurent monomial property via Theorem 6.6
nodes.section: 6.3 Positivity, $d$-vectors and linear independence of cluster monomials

nodes.name: Fix a cluster monomial not in $CM(t_0)$
nodes.statement:
Let ${\bf x}_t$, ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ be any two clusters of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$, and ${\bf x}_t^{\bf a}=\prod\limits_{i=1}^{n}x_{i;t}^{a_i}$ be a cluster monomial in $CM(t)\setminus CM(t_0)$, i.e.,  there exists $a_k>0$ such that $x_{k;t}$
is not a cluster variable in ${\bf x}_{t_0}$.

By the positivity of cluster variables, the expansion of ${\bf x}_t^{\bf a}$ with respect to ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ has the form of
\begin{eqnarray}
{\bf x}_t^{\bf a}=\sum\limits_{{\bf v}\in V} c_{\bf v}{\bf x}_{t_0}^{\bf v},\nonumber
 \end{eqnarray}
 where $V$ is a finite subset of $\mathbb Z^n$, and $0\neq c_{\bf v}\in\mathbb {NP}$ for  ${\bf v}\in V$.
  For the same reason, there exist polynomials $f_1,\cdots,f_n\in \mathbb {NP}[x_{1;t},\cdots,x_{n;t}]$ with $x_{j;t}\nmid f_i$ such that
 $$x_{i;t_0}=\frac{f_i(x_{1;t},\cdots,x_{n;t})}{{\bf x}_t^{d^t(x_{i;t_0})}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Fix a cluster monomial not in $CM(t_0)$; positive expansions in both directions
nodes.section: 6.3 Positivity, $d$-vectors and linear independence of cluster monomials

nodes.name: Substitute and clear denominators
nodes.statement:
Denote by $F^{\bf v}=f_1^{v_1}\cdots f_n^{v_n}$.  Since $v_1,\cdots,v_n\in \mathbb Z$, $F^{\bf v}$ can be written in  the form of $F^{\bf v}=\frac{F_{1;{\bf v}}}{F_{2;{\bf v}}}$, where
$F_{1;{\bf v}}, F_{2;{\bf v}}\in \mathbb {NP}[x_{1;t},\cdots,x_{n;t}]$  with $x_{j;t}\nmid F_{1;{\bf v}}$ and $x_{j;t}\nmid F_{2;{\bf v}}$, $j=1,2,\cdots,n$.
 Thus, $${\bf x}_t^{\bf a}=\sum\limits_{{\bf v}\in V} c_{\bf v}{\bf x}_{t_0}^{\bf v}=
\sum\limits_{{\bf v}\in V} c_{\bf v}{\bf x}_{t}^{-D_{t_0}^{t}\bf v}F^{\bf v}=\sum\limits_{{\bf v}\in V} c_{\bf v}{\bf x}_{t}^{-D_{t_0}^{t}\bf v}\frac{F_{1;{\bf v}}}{F_{2;{\bf v}}}.$$
 From the above equality, we can obtain an equality with the following form:
 $$
{\bf x}_t^{\bf a}g(x_{1;t},\cdots,x_{n;t})=\sum\limits_{{\bf v}\in V} c_{\bf v}{\bf x}_{t}^{-D_{t_0}^{t}{\bf v}}g_{\bf v}(x_{1;t},\cdots,x_{n;t}),
$$
which can be written as
$$g(x_{1;t},\cdots,x_{n;t})=\sum\limits_{{\bf v}\in V} c_{\bf v}{\bf x}_{t}^{-D_{t_0}^{t}{\bf v}-{\bf a}}g_{\bf v}(x_{1;t},\cdots,x_{n;t}).$$
nodes.statement_short: Substitute and clear denominators
nodes.section: 6.3 Positivity, $d$-vectors and linear independence of cluster monomials

nodes.name: Exponent constraint on the $k$-th component
nodes.statement: Because $c_{\bf v}\in\mathbb {NP}$, and $g,~g_{\bf v}\in \mathbb {NP}[x_{1;t},\cdots,x_{n;t}]$ with $x_{j;t}\nmid g$ and $x_{j;t}\nmid g_{\bf v}$ for $j=1,2,\cdots,n$, we must have $-D_{t_0}^{t}{\bf v}-{\bf a}\in\mathbb N^n$. So, the $k$-th component of  $D_{t_0}^{t}{\bf v}+{\bf a}$ satisfying $$(d_{k1}^{t_0}v_1+\cdots+d_{kn}^{t_0}v_n)+a_k\leq0,$$ where $d_{kj}^{t_0}$ is the $k$-th component of $d^t(x_{j;t_0})$, $j=1,2,\cdots,n$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponent constraint on the $k$-th component
nodes.section: 6.3 Positivity, $d$-vectors and linear independence of cluster monomials

nodes.name: Positivity of d-vectors forces ${\bf v}\notin\mathbb N^n$
nodes.statement:
By the positivity of $d$-vectors, we get that $d_{kj}^{t_0}\geq 0$, since $x_{k;t}\notin {\bf x}_{t_0}$. Then by $a_k>0$ and $(d_{k1}^{t_0}v_1+\cdots+d_{kn}^{t_0}v_n)+a_k\leq0$, we can obtain ${\bf v}\notin \mathbb N^n, {\bf v}\in V$, i.e.,
${\bf x}_t^{\bf a}$ is a sum of proper Laurent monomials in ${\bf x}_{t_0}$. So the  proper Laurent monomial property holds for $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ and thus the cluster monomials of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ are linear independence.
nodes.statement_short: Positivity of d-vectors forces ${\bf v}\notin\mathbb N^n$
nodes.section: 6.3 Positivity, $d$-vectors and linear independence of cluster monomials

nodes.name: Reduce to principal coefficients and take the g-pair partner
nodes.statement:
Thanks to Proposition \ref{proclustervariable}, we can assume that $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ is a  skew-symmetrizable cluster algebra with principal coefficients at $t_0$. By Theorem \ref{thmenough}, $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ has the enough $g$-pair property, thus for $I=\{1,2,\cdots,p\}$ and the cluster ${\bf x}_t$, there exists a cluster ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ such that $({\bf x}_t,{\bf x}_{t^\prime})$ is a $g$-pair along $I$. Thus for
 the cluster variable $x_{k;t}$ (as a cluster monomial in ${\bf x}_t$), there exists a  cluster monomial ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}^{\bf v}$ in ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ with $v_i=0$ for $i\notin I$ such that $\pi_I(g(x_{k;t}))=\pi_I(g({\bf x}_{t^\prime}^{\bf v}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to principal coefficients and take the g-pair partner along $\{1..p\}$
nodes.section: 7 Compatibility degree on the set of cluster variables

nodes.name: Sign-coherence: partner's extra entries $g'_i\ge0$
nodes.statement:
We can assume that $g(x_{k;t})=(g_1,\cdots,g_p,g_{p+1},\cdots,g_n)^{\top}$ and $g({\bf x}_{t^\prime}^{\bf v})=(g_1,\cdots,g_p,g_{p+1}^\prime,\cdots,g_n^\prime)^{\top}$.
  Because  $({\bf x}_t,{\bf x}_{t^\prime})$ is a $g$-pair along $I$, we know that ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ is a cluster connected with ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ by an $I$-sequence, and the $G$-matrix of ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ has the form of $G_{t^{\prime}}=\begin{pmatrix}G(t^{\prime})&0\\ \ast& I_{n-p}\end{pmatrix}$. By row sign-coherence of $G$-matrices, we know that $g_{p+1}^\prime,\cdots,g_n^\prime\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Sign-coherence: partner's extra entries $g'_i\ge0$
nodes.section: 7 Compatibility degree on the set of cluster variables

nodes.name: Compatibility and sign-coherence: $g_i\ge0$
nodes.statement: For each $i=p+1,p+2,\cdots,n$, since $x_{k;t}$ is compatible with $x_{i;t_0}$, there exists a cluster ${\bf x}_{t_i}$ containing both $x_{k;t}$ and $x_{i;t_0}$. By  the row sign-coherence of $G$-matrices, we know that the $i$-th row of $G_{t_i}$ is nonnegative, $i=p+1,\cdots,n$. Thus we can obtain that $g_{p+1},\cdots,g_n\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Compatibility and sign-coherence: $g_i\ge0$
nodes.section: 7 Compatibility degree on the set of cluster variables

nodes.name: Padded monomials have equal g-vectors
nodes.statement:
Then  $x_{k;t}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t}^{g_i^{\prime}}$ and ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}^{{\bf v}}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t^{\prime}}^{g_i}$ are cluster monomials in ${\bf x}_t$ and in ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}$ respectively and
\begin{eqnarray}
g(x_{k;t}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t}^{g_i^{\prime}})=(g_1,\cdots,g_p,g_{p+1}+g_{p+1}^{\prime},
\cdots,g_{n}+g_{n}^{\prime})^{\top}=g({\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}^{{\bf v}}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t^{\prime}}^{g_i}).\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
This means that the cluster monomials $x_{k;t}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t}^{g_i^{\prime}}$ and ${\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}^{{\bf v}}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t^{\prime}}^{g_i}$ have the same $g$-vector. By Theorem \ref{thmmonomial}, we get that
$$x_{k;t}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t}^{g_i^{\prime}}={\bf x}_{t^{\prime}}^{{\bf v}}\prod\limits_{i=p+1}^nx_{i;t^{\prime}}^{g_i}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Padded monomials have equal g-vectors; Theorem 3.2

nodes.name: Supports put $x_{k
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prosupport}, we get that $x_{k;t}$ is a cluster variable in ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$. Since ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ is connected with ${\bf x}_{t_0}$ by an $I=\{1,\cdots,p\}$-sequence, we know that $x_{j;t^\prime}=x_{j;t_0}$ for $j=p+1,\cdots,n$. Thus ${\bf x}_{t^\prime}$ is a cluster of $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ containing $\{x_{k;t}\}\cup\{x_{p+1;t_0},x_{p+2;t_0},\cdots,x_{n;t_0}\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Supports put $x_{k;t}$ in the partner cluster, which keeps $x_{p+1;t_0},...$

nodes.name: Write the exchange relation
nodes.statement:
By the definition of mutation, we have that

$$x_{n;t_1}x_{n;t_1}^\prime=\frac{y_{n;t_1}}{1\oplus y_{n;t_1}}\prod\limits_{b_{in}^{t_1}>0}x_{i;t_1}^{b_{in}^{t_1}}+\frac{y_{n;t_1}}{1\oplus y_{n;t_1}}\prod\limits_{b_{in}^{t_1}<0}x_{i;t_1}^{-b_{in}^{t_1}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Write the exchange relation

nodes.name: The exchange binomial has zero d-vector w.r.t. ${\bf x}_{t_2
nodes.statement:
Since $x_{i;t_1}=x_{i;t_2}$ for $i=1,2,\cdots,n-1$, we know that $\frac{y_{n;t_1}}{1\oplus y_{n;t_1}}\prod\limits_{b_{in}^{t_1}>0}x_{i;t_1}^{b_{in}^{t_1}}+\frac{y_{n;t_1}}{1\oplus y_{n;t_1}}\prod\limits_{b_{in}^{t_1}<0}x_{i;t_1}^{-b_{in}^{t_1}}$ as a polynomial in variables in ${\bf x}_{t_2}$, its $d$-vector with respect to ${\bf x}_{t_2}$ is zero, i.e., $$d^{t_2}(x_{n;t_1}x_{n;t_1}^\prime)=d^{t_2}(\frac{y_{n;t_1}}{1\oplus y_{n;t_1}}\prod\limits_{b_{in}^{t_1}>0}x_{i;t_1}^{b_{in}^{t_1}}+\frac{y_{n;t_1}}{1\oplus y_{n;t_1}}\prod\limits_{b_{in}^{t_1}<0}x_{i;t_1}^{-b_{in}^{t_1}})=0.$$
In particular, the $n$-th component of $d^{t_2}(x_{n;t_1}x_{n;t_1}^\prime)$ is zero, i.e., $d(x_{n;t_2},x_{n;t_1})+d(x_{n;t_2},x_{n;t_1}^\prime)=0.$
nodes.statement_short: The exchange binomial has zero d-vector w.r.t. ${\bf x}_{t_2}$

nodes.name: One of the two degrees is nonpositive: compatibility
nodes.statement: So, $d(x_{n;t_2},x_{n;t_1})\leq 0$ or $d(x_{n;t_2},x_{n;t_1}^\prime)\leq 0$, i.e., either that $x_{n;t_2}$ and $x_{n;t_1}$ are compatible or that   $x_{n;t_2}$ and $x_{n;t_1}^\prime$ are compatible.
nodes.statement_short: One of the two degrees is nonpositive: compatibility

nodes.name: Otherwise a compatible set of size $n+1$ contradicts Theorem
nodes.statement:
Assume that $x_{n;t_2}\neq x_{n;t_1}$ and $x_{n;t_2}\neq x_{n;t_1}^\prime$. We know that either $$\{x_{1;t_1},\cdots,x_{n-1;t_1},x_{n;t_2},x_{n;t_1}\}=\{x_{1;t_2},\cdots,x_{n-1;t_2},x_{n;t_2},x_{n;t_1}\}$$ forms a compatible set with $n+1$ elements, or $$\{x_{1;t_1},\cdots,x_{n-1;t_1},x_{n;t_2},x_{n;t_1}^\prime\}=\{x_{1;t_2},\cdots,x_{n-1;t_2},x_{n;t_2},x_{n;t_1}^\prime\}$$
forms a compatible set with $n+1$ elements. This  contradicts to Theorem \ref{thmcompatible},  so we must have $x_{n;t_2}=x_{n;t_1}$ or $x_{n;t_2}=x_{n;t_1}^\prime$.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise a compatible set of size $n+1$ contradicts Theorem 7.4
